To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the natural Trichosanthe s inhibitor has been identified and characterized, and its reaction mechanism with trypsin has been elucidated.
a peptide trypsin-inhibitor was isolated and purified by using immobilized trypsin affinity chromatog-raphy and HPLC reverse chromatography.
a peptide trypsin inhibitors from the roots of a Chinese medical herb Trichosanths kirilowii was isolated and sequenced and that it might be the smallest natural protein inhibitor so far reported.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation, purification, characterization, sequence determination, modification, and the reaction mechanism of the Tricho-santhes trypsin inhibitor.
the structure and function of the Trichostanthes trypin inhibitor, and the results are of great significance in the studies of proteinase inhibitors.
the isolation and purification, primary structure determination, and modification reaction of a natural peptide trypsin inhibitor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the natural and modified inhibitors are both potent trypsin inhibitors with different dissociation constants, and the modification of the natural inhibitor with trypin is a reversible reaction.
the natural inhibitor and its modified product have the same structure, except that the modified one lacks the C-terminal Arg residue.
the modified inhibitor has the ability to inhibit the trypsin activity, but its inhibition ability is lower than that of the natural one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the modified inhibitor is a new type of inhibitor with a new mode of action.
the natural inhibitor is a potent inhibitor for trypsin, but the modified inhibitor is an inhibitor with low activity.
the Trichosanthine trypsin inhibitor is an excellent model for studying the mechanism of enzyme inhibition and the structure-function relationship of the inhibitor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the modification of the reactive site peptide bond in the natural inhibitor can not only increase the dissociation constant of inhibitor-trypsin complex, but also reduce its inhibition activity.
the modified inhibitor is still a potent inhibitor for trypsin.
the peptide bond in the inhibitor reactive site can be cleaved by trypsin at a low pH, and the cleavage reaction is reversible.
